headline: California cannabis sales reach $987M in Q3 2026; tax take $255M
dek: California retailers sold $987 million of cannabis in the third quarter, up about 3% on a year earlier, while state tax fell 10% at the lower 15% rate.
key_points: California's tax agency reported $255.3 million in cannabis tax from third-quarter 2026 returns: $148.1 million in excise tax and $107.2 million in sales tax.
Retail sales were $987 million, against $960.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, MJBizDaily reported from the same state data.
Tax revenue was about 10% below the $283.7 million first reported for Q3 2025, when the excise rate was briefly 19% rather than 15%.
Sales for the first nine months stand at $2.965 billion; the fourth quarter would need about $1.035 billion to bring the year to $4 billion.
body: California's licensed cannabis shops sold a little more in the third quarter of 2026 than a year earlier, and the state collected a good deal less tax on it. Both facts come from data the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) released on 19 November, and both trace back to the same event: the short-lived rise in the state excise tax in 2025.

The CDTFA said cannabis retailers remitted $255.3 million in tax for the July to September quarter, made up of $148.1 million in cannabis excise tax and $107.2 million in sales tax. The figures count returns received by 17 November and leave out late and unprocessed returns, so they are likely to be revised upward. Retail sales for the quarter were $987 million, MJBizDaily reported from the agency's data.
## The numbers

Sales of $987 million compare with $960.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, a rise of about 2.8% on our calculation. Tax moved the other way. The $255.3 million total is about 10% below the $283.7 million the state first reported for the same quarter a year earlier, according to The Marijuana Herald.

Against the previous quarter, both lines slipped. The CDTFA revised its second-quarter 2026 tax figure to $262 million, from $261.7 million, after amended and late returns: $152.2 million in excise tax and $109.8 million in sales tax. Third-quarter revenue is about 2.6% below that. Second-quarter sales were $1.013 billion, MJBizDaily reported, so sales fell by a similar share, about 2.6%, from spring to summer.

Since January 2018, cannabis has generated more than $8.6 billion in state tax, the CDTFA said: more than $4.6 billion in excise tax, $3.5 billion in sales tax and $500.6 million from a cultivation tax that was abolished on 1 July 2022.
## Why tax fell while sales rose

The gap is a rate effect. In the summer of 2025 the state excise tax rose from 15% to 19% under an automatic increase written into state law, after lawmakers and the governor did not agree a budget deal to stop it, MJBizDaily reported. Governor Gavin Newsom signed a repeal in September 2025 and the rate returned to 15% on 1 October 2025, according to the Herald. So the third quarter of 2025 was taxed at 19%, and the third quarter of 2026 at 15%.

The new figures are consistent with that. Excise tax of $148.1 million on $987 million of sales works out to 15.0%. Adding sales tax, the state's two retail taxes took about 25.9% of the quarter's reported sales. That is our arithmetic from the published totals, and it excludes local cannabis taxes and fees, which vary by city and county and are not in the CDTFA release.
> California cut its rate back to 15% and sales edged up about 3%. The state gave up roughly a tenth of its tax to get there.
## Is the market recovering?

MJBizDaily's reading is that sales are stabilising after the tax increase pushed annual sales to just under $4 billion in 2025. The second quarter of 2026 ran slightly ahead of the second quarter of 2025, $1.013 billion against $1.006 billion, and the third quarter did the same. Through September, 2026 sales total $2.965 billion, about $20 million more than the first nine months of 2025.

There are limits to the good news. The outlet notes that $987 million is still the fourth-lowest quarterly figure since the market matured. And revenue understates activity: falling prices mean shops ring up more items for less money. A flat dollar figure in a market with price compression can hide rising volume, which is better news for consumers than for operators' margins.

For the full year to reach $4 billion, the fourth quarter would need about $1.035 billion in sales, on our calculation. That would be the strongest quarter of the year. The fourth quarter includes the holiday period, but nothing in the state data yet shows that pace.
## What operators say is still wrong

California banned sales of intoxicating hemp products outside licensed cannabis channels more than two years ago, well before the federal cap due on 11 December, so licensed retailers there do not face the unregulated hemp competition seen in other states, MJBizDaily noted. Operators' main complaint remains cost: local taxes and fees stacked on top of state excise and sales tax, which they say keep the illicit market cheaper. In Los Angeles, mayor-elect Nithya Raman pledged during the campaign to rewrite a city fee structure that local operators have called disastrous, according to the outlet.

The excise tax funds childcare and early childhood programmes, medical research, youth substance-abuse prevention and environmental work, the CDTFA said. That creates a standing tension in Sacramento: the programmes that depend on the tax took a cut of roughly a tenth, year on year, even as the industry argued the lower rate was needed to keep licensed shops alive.
## What it means

For operators, the data supports a narrow claim: at 15%, sales stopped falling. It does not show strong growth, and the comparison quarter in 2025 was depressed by the higher rate, which flatters the year-on-year number. For other states weighing rate changes, California now offers a rough natural experiment, with one caveat: a single year of quarterly data cannot separate the tax effect from price declines and consumer spending more broadly.
## What to watch

Watch for the CDTFA's revision of the third-quarter figures when fourth-quarter data is published; the second-quarter figure was revised up this time. Watch the fourth-quarter sales total against the $1.035 billion needed for a $4 billion year. In Los Angeles, watch for the incoming mayor's proposals on cannabis fees. And watch the 2027 state budget talks for any attempt to revisit the excise rate.
